## Study Design, Biomedical Cohorts, and Synthetic Ground-Truth Regimes

We evaluate the `{python} N.n_models_word` benchmarked architectures defined in Chapter 2 across twelve multi-view benchmarks: six real biomedical and clinical cohorts (`ADNI-MCI`, `MultiOmics` [TCGA-BRCA], `TCGA-KIRC`, `Heart`, `Diabetes`, and `mfeat`) and six synthetic generative regimes with known ground-truth latent coordinates $\mathbf{U}^*$ and feature supports $\mathbf{V}_m^*$ (@tbl-benchmark-cohorts). Every model is evaluated across three independent 70/30 stratified or random train/test splits (seeds $42, 43, 44$) across three `nsa_flow` quantile sparsity levels ($q \in \{\text{None}, 0.5, 0.8\}$, `{python} N.n_default_fits` train/test fits), plus `{python} N.n_positive_reruns` paired reruns with non-negative loadings on the three high-dimensional cohorts and a `{python} N.sweep_n`-configuration hyperparameter sweep on `ADNI-MCI` ($N = 1,084$, one seed). To prevent data leakage, all feature standardization (`StandardScaler`), column completeness filtering ($\ge 98\%$), and demographic covariate adjustments (Frisch–Waugh–Lovell residualization [@frisch1933partial; @lovell1963seasonal] of age, biological sex, and education inside `ADNI-MCI`) are fitted strictly within each training split and applied out-of-sample to the held-out test split.

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| label: tbl-benchmark-cohorts
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of the twelve multi-view benchmark cohorts (six clinical/biomedical datasets and six synthetic ground-truth generative regimes). Best out-of-sample scores across seeds 42–44 are computed directly from `deep_ranking_benchmark.csv`."
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import os
import pandas as pd
from tabulate import tabulate

csv_path = "results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_path):
    csv_path = "paper/results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"

df = pd.read_csv(csv_path)
df["Model"] = df["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})

cohort_meta = [
    ("ADNI-MCI", "Clinical MRI + Cog", 1084, "4 [160, 160, 62, 11]", "CogPC1 R2 (MRI Only)"),
    ("MultiOmics (BRCA)", "Oncology (mRNA/CNV/RPPA)", 822, "3 [200, 150, 150]", "ER Status Accuracy"),
    ("TCGA-KIRC", "Oncology (mRNA/CNV/RPPA)", 467, "3 [200, 150, 150]", "Pathologic Stage Acc"),
    ("Diabetes", "Clinical Chemistries", 442, "2 [5, 5]", "1-Yr Progression R2"),
    ("Heart", "Cardiology Vitals + ECG", 297, "2 [7, 6]", "Coronary Disease Acc"),
    ("mfeat", "Multi-Descriptor Digits", 2000, "4 [76, 64, 6, 47]", "10-Class Accuracy"),
    ("Linear", "Synthetic (50% Sparse ±)", 1000, "3 [100, 80, 60]", "Latent R2 & Support F1"),
    ("Polynomial", "Synthetic (Deg-3 Warped)", 1000, "3 [120, 80, 50]", "Latent R2 & CMC"),
    ("Sine", "Synthetic (Harmonic Warp)", 1000, "3 [120, 80, 50]", "Latent R2 & CMC"),
    ("Shared+Private", "Synthetic (80% Sparse ±)", 1000, "3 [160, 60, 30]", "Latent R2 & Support F1"),
    ("NonnegParts", "Synthetic (66.7% Non-Neg)", 400, "3 [120, 45, 30]", "Dominant Factor R2 & F1"),
    ("NonnegWeak", "Synthetic (80% Non-Neg)", 400, "3 [120, 45, 30]", "Weak Factor u3 R2 & F1"),
]

rows = []
for ds_label, domain, n_subj, views_str, task_str in cohort_meta:
    if "MultiOmics" in ds_label:
        ds_key = "MultiOmics"
    elif ds_label == "NonnegWeak":
        ds_key = "NonnegPartsWeak"
    else:
        ds_key = ds_label
    sub = df[df["Dataset"] == ds_key]
    agg_xv = sub.groupby("Model")["Strictly_Linear_Metric"].mean()
    pca_v = agg_xv["PCA"]
    best_m = agg_xv.idxmax()
    best_v = agg_xv.max()
    rows.append([
        ds_label,
        domain,
        f"{n_subj:,}",
        views_str,
        task_str,
        f"{best_m} ({best_v:.3f} vs PCA {pca_v:.3f})"
    ])

headers = ["Cohort", "Domain / Modality Structure", "N", "Views [p_m]", "Clinical / Task Target", "Best Linear XV vs PCA"]
print(tabulate(rows, headers=headers, tablefmt="pipe"))
```

In `ADNI-MCI` ($N = 1,084$) [@mueller2005; @jack2008alzheimer; @ADNI], Views 0–2 capture $382$ regional structural MRI features derived via the ANTs longitudinal and cross-sectional cortical thickness and Desikan–Killiany–Tourville (DKT) parcellation pipelines [@avants2008symmetric; @avants2011reproducible; @tustison2014large; @desikan2006automated; @klein2012mindboggle; @stone2020longitudinal; @stone2024blast; @Marek2011; @smith2013functional], while View 3 comprises eleven neuropsychological scales (`ADAS11`, `ADAS13`, `ADASQ4` [@rosen1984new], `MMSE` [@folstein1975mini], `CDRSB` [@morris1993clinical], `TRABSCOR` [@reitan1958validity], `FAQ` [@pfeffer1982measurement], and four Rey Auditory Verbal Learning Test sub-scores `RAVLT_immediate`, `RAVLT_learning`, `RAVLT_forgetting`, `RAVLT_perc_forgetting` [@rey1964examen]). Following `Protocol B`, the three MRI views align with the cognitive battery during training, but test-set predictions are generated exclusively from structural MRI. In `MultiOmics` (`TCGA-BRCA`, $N = 822$) [@tcga2012breast] and `TCGA-KIRC` ($N = 467$) [@tcga2013kirc], mRNA expression ($p_1 = 200$), somatic copy-number variation ($p_2 = 150$), and RPPA proteomics ($p_3 = 150$) predict clinical Estrogen Receptor status and pathologic tumor stage, respectively.

## Global 12-Dataset Benchmark: Subspace Capacity vs. Single-Axis Interpretability

Across the $B = 12$ dataset blocks and `{python} N.n_models_word` architectures, block-averaged non-parametric Friedman [@friedman1937use] and Iman–Davenport [@Iman1980] omnibus tests differentiate the `{python} N.n_models_word` models on both the linear subspace probe ($\chi_F^2 =$ `{python} N.fr_lin_chi2`, $p =$ `{python} N.fr_lin_p`; $F_F =$ `{python} N.fr_lin_F`, $p =$ `{python} N.fr_lin_pF`) and the multi-modal consensus probe ($\chi_F^2 =$ `{python} N.fr_u_chi2`, $p =$ `{python} N.fr_u_p`; $F_F =$ `{python} N.fr_u_F`, $p =$ `{python} N.fr_u_pF`; Nemenyi Critical Difference $CD =$ `{python} N.cd` at $\alpha = 0.05$ [@Demsar2006; @Nemenyi1963; @benavoli2016should]). @tbl-global-leaderboard summarizes the global metrics across all `{python} N.n_models_word` models, accompanied by the Demšar Critical Difference diagram (@fig-cd-diagram), the multi-objective speed–accuracy and support–consensus Pareto frontiers (@fig-pareto-frontier), and the three-probe performance profile (@fig-three-probes).

import os
import sys
import pandas as pd
from tabulate import tabulate

csv_main = "results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_main):
    csv_main = "paper/results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"

csv_op = "results_cache/operating_points_05_08_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_op):
    csv_op = "paper/results_cache/operating_points_05_08_benchmark.csv"

df_main = pd.read_csv(csv_main)
df_main["Model"] = df_main["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})

from paper_numbers import op_default
df_op = op_default()  # default positivity only; the paired positive reruns would double-weight 3 cohorts
sub05 = df_op[df_op["Sparseness_Target"] == 0.5]

repo_root = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "..")) if "paper" in os.getcwd() else os.getcwd()
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(repo_root, "src"))
from pysimlr.benchmarks.deep_ranking import build_ranking_blocks, friedman_test

piv_xv, _ = build_ranking_blocks(df_main, metric_col="Strictly_Linear_Metric", floor_threshold=None)
f_xv = friedman_test(piv_xv.values, higher_is_better=True)
ranks_xv = pd.Series(f_xv["mean_ranks"], index=piv_xv.columns)

syn_df = sub05[sub05["Case_Type"] == "synthetic"]
syn_f1 = syn_df.groupby("Model")["Support_Recovery_V"].mean()
syn_cmc = df_main[df_main["Case_Type"] == "synthetic"].groupby("Model")["CMC_Latent_U"].mean()

agg05 = sub05.groupby("Model").agg({
    "Strictly_Linear_Metric": "mean",
    "Axis_Sensitive_Metric": "mean",
    "Predictive_Metric": "mean",
    "Sparsity_Ratio": "mean",
    "Fit_Seconds": "mean"
})

order = ranks_xv.sort_values().index.tolist()
rows = []
for m in order:
    lin_v = agg05.loc[m, "Strictly_Linear_Metric"]
    rf_v = agg05.loc[m, "Axis_Sensitive_Metric"]
    u_v = agg05.loc[m, "Predictive_Metric"]
    drop_v = rf_v - lin_v
    rows.append([
        m,
        f"{ranks_xv[m]:.2f}",
        f"{lin_v:.3f}",
        f"{rf_v:.3f} ({drop_v:+.3f})",
        f"{u_v:.3f}",
        f"{syn_cmc[m]:.3f}",
        f"{syn_f1[m]:.3f}",
        f"{agg05.loc[m, 'Sparsity_Ratio']*100:.1f}%"
    ])

headers = [
    "Architecture", "Friedman Rank ↓", "Linear XV ↑", "RF Axis XV (Drop) ↑",
    "Consensus U ↑", "Latent CMC ↑", "Support F1 ↑", "Sparsity % ↑"
]
print(tabulate(rows, headers=headers, tablefmt="pipe"))

#| warning: false

#| fig-cap: "Demšar (2006) Critical Difference diagram across the $B = 12$ benchmark dataset blocks (seeds averaged within each dataset) for the linear entrypoint probe ($\\mathbf{X}\\mathbf{V}$; Friedman and Iman–Davenport statistics in the text). Horizontal axis plots mean rank (lower is better, $1 =$ best). Bold horizontal bars connect cliques of architectures whose rank differences are smaller than the Nemenyi Critical Difference ($\\alpha = 0.05$). Green stars (`*`) indicate models on the 5-objective non-dominated Pareto frontier."
#| out-width: 100%
#| echo: false
import os
import sys
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

csv_main = "results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_main):
    csv_main = "paper/results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"

df_main = pd.read_csv(csv_main)
df_main["Model"] = df_main["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})

repo_root = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "..")) if "paper" in os.getcwd() else os.getcwd()
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(repo_root, "src"))
from pysimlr.benchmarks.deep_ranking import build_ranking_blocks, friedman_test, compute_nemenyi_cd, compute_pareto_frontier

piv_xv, _ = build_ranking_blocks(df_main, metric_col="Strictly_Linear_Metric", floor_threshold=None)
f_xv = friedman_test(piv_xv.values, higher_is_better=True)
ranks = pd.Series(f_xv["mean_ranks"], index=piv_xv.columns).sort_values()
cd = compute_nemenyi_cd(piv_xv.shape[1], piv_xv.shape[0])

agg_all = df_main.groupby("Model", as_index=False).agg({
    "Predictive_Metric": "mean",
    "Strictly_Linear_Metric": "mean",
    "CMC_Latent_U": "mean",
    "Support_Recovery_V": "mean",
    "Fit_Seconds": "mean"
})
pareto_df = compute_pareto_frontier(
    agg_all,
    objectives=["Predictive_Metric", "Strictly_Linear_Metric", "CMC_Latent_U", "Support_Recovery_V", "Fit_Seconds"],
    maximize=[True, True, True, True, False]
)
pareto_set = set(pareto_df[pareto_df["is_pareto_optimal"]]["Model"])

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10.5, 3.6), dpi=300)
ax.set_xlim(0.3, 9.7)
ax.set_ylim(0.0, 1.25)
ax.axis("off")

# Number line 1..9
y_axis = 0.92
ax.plot([1, 9], [y_axis, y_axis], color="#0f172a", lw=1.8)
for r_tick in range(1, 10):
    ax.plot([r_tick, r_tick], [y_axis - 0.035, y_axis + 0.035], color="#0f172a", lw=1.4)
    ax.text(r_tick, y_axis + 0.06, str(r_tick), ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9.5, weight="bold", color="#0f172a")

# Nemenyi CD reference bar at top left
cd_x0 = 1.0
cd_y = 1.15
ax.plot([cd_x0, cd_x0 + cd], [cd_y, cd_y], color="#dc2626", lw=2.4)
ax.plot([cd_x0, cd_x0], [cd_y - 0.03, cd_y + 0.03], color="#dc2626", lw=1.8)
ax.plot([cd_x0 + cd, cd_x0 + cd], [cd_y - 0.03, cd_y + 0.03], color="#dc2626", lw=1.8)
ax.text(cd_x0 + cd / 2, cd_y + 0.035, f"Nemenyi CD = {cd:.2f} (α = 0.05)", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9.0, weight="bold", color="#dc2626")

# Split models into left (top 5) and right (bottom 4)
n_left = 5
left_models = list(ranks.index[:n_left])
right_models = list(ranks.index[n_left:])

y_positions_left = np.linspace(0.62, 0.10, len(left_models))
for idx_m, m in enumerate(left_models):
    r_val = ranks[m]
    y_m = y_positions_left[idx_m]
    is_p = m in pareto_set
    col_m = "#059669" if is_p else "#0f172a"
    star = " *" if is_p else ""
    ax.plot([r_val, r_val], [y_axis, y_m], color="#475569", lw=1.1, linestyle="-")
    ax.plot([r_val, 0.85], [y_m, y_m], color="#475569", lw=1.1, linestyle="-")
    ax.plot(r_val, y_axis, "o", color=col_m, markersize=6.5)
    ax.text(0.80, y_m, f"{m}{star} ({r_val:.2f})", ha="right", va="center", fontsize=9.0, weight="bold", color=col_m)

y_positions_right = np.linspace(0.62, 0.16, len(right_models))
for idx_m, m in enumerate(right_models):
    r_val = ranks[m]
    y_m = y_positions_right[idx_m]
    is_p = m in pareto_set
    col_m = "#059669" if is_p else "#0f172a"
    star = " *" if is_p else ""
    ax.plot([r_val, r_val], [y_axis, y_m], color="#475569", lw=1.1, linestyle="-")
    ax.plot([r_val, 9.15], [y_m, y_m], color="#475569", lw=1.1, linestyle="-")
    ax.plot(r_val, y_axis, "o", color=col_m, markersize=6.5)
    ax.text(9.20, y_m, f"({r_val:.2f}) {m}{star}", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=9.0, weight="bold", color=col_m)

# Clique bars
r_vals = ranks.values
cliques = []
for i in range(len(r_vals)):
    j = i
    while j + 1 < len(r_vals) and (r_vals[j + 1] - r_vals[i]) <= cd:
        j += 1
    if j > i:
        is_sub = any(c_i <= i and j <= c_j for c_i, c_j in cliques)
        if not is_sub:
            cliques.append((i, j))

clique_y_base = 0.81
for c_idx, (i, j) in enumerate(cliques):
    cy = clique_y_base - c_idx * 0.065
    ax.plot([r_vals[i], r_vals[j]], [cy, cy], color="#1e293b", lw=4.0, solid_capstyle="round")

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

#| out-width: 100%

import os
import sys
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

csv_main = "results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_main):
    csv_main = "paper/results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"

df_main = pd.read_csv(csv_main)
df_main["Model"] = df_main["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})

repo_root = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "..")) if "paper" in os.getcwd() else os.getcwd()
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(repo_root, "src"))
from pysimlr.benchmarks.deep_ranking import compute_pareto_frontier

agg_all = df_main.groupby("Model", as_index=False).agg({
    "Predictive_Metric": "mean",
    "Strictly_Linear_Metric": "mean",
    "CMC_Latent_U": "mean",
    "Support_Recovery_V": "mean",
    "Fit_Seconds": "mean"
})
p_df = compute_pareto_frontier(
    agg_all,
    objectives=["Predictive_Metric", "Strictly_Linear_Metric", "CMC_Latent_U", "Support_Recovery_V", "Fit_Seconds"],
    maximize=[True, True, True, True, False]
).set_index("Model")
syn_sub = df_main[df_main["Case_Type"] == "synthetic"].groupby("Model")[["CMC_Latent_U", "Support_Recovery_V"]].mean()

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11.2, 4.3), dpi=300, constrained_layout=True)

# Panel A: Consensus U vs Fit_Seconds
for m, row in p_df.iterrows():
    is_p = bool(row["is_pareto_optimal"])
    marker = "*" if is_p else "o"
    sz = 150 if is_p else 75
    col = "#059669" if is_p else "#475569"
    ax1.scatter(row["Fit_Seconds"], row["Predictive_Metric"], marker=marker, s=sz, color=col, edgecolor="#0f172a", lw=0.8, zorder=4)

offsets_a = {
    "PCA": (-28, -3),
    "NSAFlow-PCA": (8, 5),
    "SiMLR": (8, -4),
    "LEND": (-14, 9),
    "NED": (-28, -10),
    "NEDPP": (8, 4),
    "Flow-SiMR-V": (-62, -14),
}
for m, row in p_df.iterrows():
    dx, dy = offsets_a.get(m, (6, 4))
    col_t = "#065f46" if row["is_pareto_optimal"] else "#1e293b"
    ax1.annotate(m, (row["Fit_Seconds"], row["Predictive_Metric"]), xytext=(dx, dy), textcoords="offset points", fontsize=8.2, weight="bold", color=col_t)

front_a = p_df.loc[RAW["pareto_2d_models"]]  # 2D speed-accuracy frontier, computed in paper_numbers
ax1.plot(front_a["Fit_Seconds"], front_a["Predictive_Metric"], "--", color="#059669", lw=1.6, alpha=0.8, label="2D Speed–Accuracy Envelope")

ax1.set_xscale("log")
ax1.set_xlim(0.0005, 13.5)
ax1.set_ylim(0.535, 0.725)
ax1.set_xlabel("Mean Fit Time in Seconds (Log Scale, ↓ Faster)", fontsize=9.5, weight="bold")
ax1.set_ylabel("Out-of-Sample Consensus Score (U ↑)", fontsize=9.5, weight="bold")
ax1.set_title("A. Consensus Accuracy vs. Fit Time", fontsize=10.2, weight="bold")
ax1.grid(True, linestyle="--", alpha=0.35)
ax1.legend(loc="lower left", fontsize=8.2, frameon=True)

# Panel B: Support F1 vs CMC on Synthetic Regimes
for m in syn_sub.index:
    is_p = bool(p_df.loc[m, "is_pareto_optimal"])
    marker = "*" if is_p else "o"
    sz = 150 if is_p else 75
    col = "#059669" if is_p else "#475569"
    ax2.scatter(syn_sub.loc[m, "CMC_Latent_U"], syn_sub.loc[m, "Support_Recovery_V"], marker=marker, s=sz, color=col, edgecolor="#0f172a", lw=0.8, zorder=4)

offsets_b = {
    "SiMLR": (8, -2),
    "NSAFlow-PCA": (-48, -15),
    "LEND": (8, 6),
    "NED": (-30, -3),
    "NEDPP": (7, 4),
    "Flow-SiMR-V": (8, -6),
    "PCA": (8, 4),
}
for m in syn_sub.index:
    dx, dy = offsets_b.get(m, (6, 4))
    col_t = "#065f46" if p_df.loc[m, "is_pareto_optimal"] else "#1e293b"
    ax2.annotate(m, (syn_sub.loc[m, "CMC_Latent_U"], syn_sub.loc[m, "Support_Recovery_V"]), xytext=(dx, dy), textcoords="offset points", fontsize=8.2, weight="bold", color=col_t)

ax2.set_xlim(0.32, 0.95)
ax2.set_ylim(-0.04, 0.74)
ax2.set_xlabel("Latent Manifold Recovery on U (CMC ↑)", fontsize=9.5, weight="bold")
ax2.set_ylabel("Pathway Support Recovery on V (Jaccard F1 ↑)", fontsize=9.5, weight="bold")
ax2.set_title("B. Sparse Support Recovery vs. Latent Manifold CMC", fontsize=10.2, weight="bold")
ax2.grid(True, linestyle="--", alpha=0.35)

plt.show()

#| out-width: 100%

import os
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

csv_op = "results_cache/operating_points_05_08_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_op):
    csv_op = "paper/results_cache/operating_points_05_08_benchmark.csv"

from paper_numbers import op_default
df_op = op_default()  # default positivity only

sub05 = df_op[df_op["Sparseness_Target"] == 0.5]
piv_probes = sub05.groupby("Model")[["Strictly_Linear_Metric", "Axis_Sensitive_Metric", "Predictive_Metric"]].mean()
model_order = ["LEND", "Flow-SiMR-V", "SiMLR", "NEDPP", "NED", "NSAFlow-PCA", "PCA"]
piv_probes = piv_probes.reindex([m for m in model_order if m in piv_probes.index])

fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(10.8, 3.9), dpi=300)

x = np.arange(len(piv_probes))
width = 0.26
b1 = ax1.bar(x - width, piv_probes["Strictly_Linear_Metric"], width, label="1. Subspace Fidelity: Ridge(XV) ↑", color="#0284c7", edgecolor="#0f172a", lw=0.7)
b2 = ax1.bar(x, piv_probes["Axis_Sensitive_Metric"], width, label="2. Single-Axis Interpretability: RandomForest(XV) ↑", color="#0d9488", edgecolor="#0f172a", lw=0.7)
b3 = ax1.bar(x + width, piv_probes["Predictive_Metric"], width, label="3. Multi-Modal Consensus: Ridge(U) ↑", color="#d97706", edgecolor="#0f172a", lw=0.7)

for bars in (b1, b2, b3):
    for bar in bars:
        h = bar.get_height()
        ax1.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2, h + 0.004, f"{h:.2f}", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=7.2, weight="bold", color="#1e293b")

ax1.set_ylabel("Mean Out-of-Sample Score (↑)", fontsize=9.8, weight="bold")
ax1.set_title("Three-Probe Performance Profile Across 12 Benchmarks (Operating Point q = 0.5)", fontsize=10.5, weight="bold")
ax1.set_xticks(x)
ax1.set_xticklabels(piv_probes.index, fontsize=9.0, weight="bold", rotation=15, ha="right")
ax1.set_ylim(0.50, 0.76)
ax1.grid(True, axis="y", linestyle="--", alpha=0.35)
ax1.legend(loc="upper right", frameon=True, fontsize=8.5, ncol=3)

pca_idx = list(piv_probes.index).index("PCA")
_drop = piv_probes["Axis_Sensitive_Metric"] - piv_probes["Strictly_Linear_Metric"]
ax1.annotate(f"PCA axis-mixing drop\n(RF − linear = {_drop['PCA']:+.3f}; SiMLR {_drop['SiMLR']:+.3f})",
             xy=(pca_idx, piv_probes.loc["PCA", "Axis_Sensitive_Metric"]),
             xytext=(pca_idx - 2.6, 0.535),
             arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color="#dc2626", lw=1.5),
             fontsize=8.3, weight="bold", color="#dc2626",
             bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", fc="#fef2f2", ec="#fca5a5", lw=1.0))

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Three empirical principles emerge from @tbl-global-leaderboard and Figures [-@fig-cd-diagram]–[-@fig-three-probes]:

1. **Multi-View Alignment Against Single-Matrix Factorization**: The leading mean Friedman ranks on the linear entrypoint probe are `{python} N.rank_lin_top4`, against `PCA` (`{python} N.rank_lin_PCA`) and `NSAFlow-PCA` (`{python} N.rank_lin_NSAFlow_PCA`). On heterogeneous cohorts such as `mfeat` ($p = [76, 64, 6, 47]$) and `Shared+Private` ($p = [160, 60, 30]$), concatenated `PCA` reaches a linear score of `{python} N.mfeat_pca` (`mfeat` accuracy) and `{python} N.sp_pca` (`Shared+Private` $R^2$), against `{python} N.mfeat_best` (`{python} N.mfeat_best_model`) and `{python} N.sp_best` (`{python} N.sp_best_model`) for the best multi-view model. Over the 12 datasets (seeds averaged, Wilcoxon signed-rank against `PCA` with Holm adjustment, Appendix B), the linear score differs from `PCA` at $p < 0.05$ for `{python} N.wilcoxon_n_sig` of 8 models: `{python} N.wilcoxon_sig`.
2. **Coordinate Alignment and the Random Forest Axis Drop**: As established in @eq-subspace-invariance, ridge regression on $\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ is insensitive to orthogonal or oblique column mixing $\mathbf{V}_m \mathbf{M}$, hiding the fact that dense `PCA` mixes distinct mechanisms across columns. With coordinate-splitting decision trees (`RandomForest`), `PCA` loses `{python} N.drop_pca` on average across the 12 cohorts (Random Forest minus linear score), falling from `{python} N.npw_pca` to `{python} N.npw_pca_rf` on the weak sparse factors of `NonnegPartsWeak` and from `{python} N.adni_pca` to `{python} N.adni_pca_rf` on `ADNI-MCI` (`{python} N.adni_pca_rf_drop_pct` lower). The smallest drops are `{python} N.drop_best_models`.
3. **Operating Points and Feature Density ($q = 0.5$ vs. $q = 0.8$)**: @fig-operating-point-and-support shows the quantile threshold $q$ as a lens on feature support recovery. Across the `{python} N.n_default_fits` default-positivity fits, the mean linear score is `{python} N.op_lin_None`, `{python} N.op_lin_05` and `{python} N.op_lin_08` at $q = \text{None}$, $0.5$ and $0.8$, and the mean Random Forest axis score is `{python} N.op_rf_None`, `{python} N.op_rf_05` and `{python} N.op_rf_08`; at $q = 0.8$, `{python} N.op_sparsity_08` of loadings are zero while `{python} N.op_retained_08` of the best linear score is retained. At $q = 0.5$, support recovery on the $50\%$-sparse `Linear` regime ranges from $F_1 =$ `{python} N.f1_linear_q05_min` (`{python} N.f1_linear_q05_min_model`) to `{python} N.f1_linear_q05_max` (`{python} N.f1_linear_q05_max_model`), and reaches `{python} N.f1_np_q05_best` on `NonnegParts` (`{python} N.f1_np_q05_best_model`). On the focal $20\%$-active modules, the best $F_1$ at $q = 0.8$ is `{python} N.f1_npw_q08_best` on `NonnegPartsWeak` (`{python} N.f1_npw_q08_best_model`) and `{python} N.f1_sp_q08_best` on `Shared+Private` (`{python} N.f1_sp_q08_best_model`).

## Clinical Neuroimaging in `ADNI-MCI` ($N = 1,084$): Predicting Cognitive Decline and Mapping Braak Staging from MRI Alone

A primary clinical test of multi-modal representation learning is whether aligning structural neuroimaging with multi-domain cognitive batteries during training yields an anatomical basis that better predicts cognitive severity in new patients who have only undergone an MRI scan (`Protocol B`). Across $N = 1,084$ participants with Mild Cognitive Impairment, @tbl-adni-mci-summary compares all `{python} N.n_models_word` benchmark models on held-out MRI-only prediction of composite cognitive impairment (`CogPC1` $R^2$, after in-fold adjustment for age, sex, and education), single-axis Random Forest prediction, and mean ridge regression $R^2$ across all eleven individual neuropsychological scales (`ADAS11`, `ADAS13`, `ADASQ4`, `MMSE`, `CDRSB`, `TRABSCOR`, `FAQ`, and four `RAVLT` memory scales).

]

Comparing the unsupervised anatomical baselines against cognitive-aligned SiMR models in @tbl-adni-mci-summary and @fig-adni-neuroanatomy-flagship yields three findings:

1. **Supervising MRI Factor Discovery with Cognitive Batteries Improves Out-of-Sample MRI Prediction**: Unsupervised `PCA` on the $382$ structural MRI features explains $R^2 =$ `{python} N.adni_pca` $\pm$ `{python} N.adni_pca_sd` of out-of-sample cognitive variance (`CogPC1`) on the linear probe and `{python} N.adni_pca_rf` on the single-axis Random Forest probe. Aligning the MRI projections with the 11-scale cognitive battery during training gives, for the four leading models (3-seed means $\pm$ SD), `{python} N.adni_ranked`; the best is `{python} N.adni_gain_pct` over `PCA`. The best single-axis Random Forest score is `{python} N.adni_rf_best` (`{python} N.adni_rf_best_model`), `{python} N.adni_rf_ratio` times that of `PCA`. In the single-seed sweep the best configuration reaches `{python} N.sweep_best_r2` (`{python} N.sweep_best_model`) and the best linear-family configuration `{python} N.sweep_linear_best_r2` (`{python} N.sweep_linear_best_model`), against `{python} N.sweep_pca_r2` for `PCA`; mean prediction across all eleven scales reaches `{python} N.sweep_m11_best` (`{python} N.sweep_m11_best_model`) against `{python} N.sweep_m11_pca` for `PCA` (`{python} N.sweep_m11_gain`). These sweep peaks are maxima over many configurations on one split and are optimistic.
2. **Varimax Rotation and Quantile Sparsity on Cortical Thickness**: @fig-adni-neuroanatomy-flagship shows the 62 DKT cortical-thickness loadings (single seed, `Protocol B`, `SiMLR`, $w = 0.50$). Dense `PCA` (Panel A1) has `{python} N.fl_pca_sp` zero loadings. Non-negative SiMR without rotation or quantile thresholding (Panel A2, `varimax = False, q = None`) is `{python} N.fl_col_pca_simr_sp` sparse with `{python} N.fl_col_pca_simr_active` active regions per component; with Varimax rotation (Panel A3, `varimax = True, q = None`) it is `{python} N.fl_varimax_simr_sp` sparse with `{python} N.fl_varimax_simr_active`. With `sparseness = 0.85` (Panels A4 and B) each component keeps `{python} N.fl_col_pca_q85_simr_active` regions (`{python} N.fl_col_pca_q85_simr_sp` sparse, Gram defect $D =$ `{python} N.fl_q85_D`) with out-of-sample `CogPC1` $R^2 =$ `{python} N.fl_col_pca_q85_simr_r2`, against `{python} N.fl_pca_r2` for `PCA` on the same split. The leading regions of each component are:
   * **Component 1 ($\mathbf{v}_1$)**: `{python} N.fl_q85_c1_top`.
   * **Component 2 ($\mathbf{v}_2$)**: `{python} N.fl_q85_c2_top`.
   * **Component 3 ($\mathbf{v}_3$)**: `{python} N.fl_q85_c3_top`.
3. **Support-Shuffled and PCA-Rotated Score Controls**: The largest weight on primary motor or somatosensory cortex (`precentral`, `postcentral`) at $q = 0.85$ is `{python} N.fl_sensorimotor_max`. To separate coordinate-level axis alignment and anatomical support localization from subspace capacity, two negative controls are evaluated across 3 seeds on `ADNI-MCI` (`adni_mci_axis_alignment_controls.csv`, `axis_alignment_control_metrics`): (i) a **PCA-Rotated Score Control** rotates the learned scores $\mathbf{Z} = [\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m]$ by their in-fold principal-component eigenvectors, which leaves the linear probe unchanged (largest difference `{python} N.ctl_linear_invariance`) and lowers the single-axis Random Forest score for `{python} N.ctl_rot_n_lower` of `{python} N.ctl_n_models` models; (ii) a **Support-Shuffled Basis Control** permutes the rows of each $\mathbf{V}_m$ within its view, preserving sparsity, weight magnitudes and $\mathbf{V}_m^\top \mathbf{V}_m$, and lowers the Random Forest `CogPC1` $R^2$ for `{python} N.ctl_shuffle_n_lower` of `{python} N.ctl_n_models` models: `{python} N.ctl_shuffle_lowers`. Unshuffled Random Forest scores are `{python} N.ctl_rf_ratio_min`–`{python} N.ctl_rf_ratio_max` times that of `PCA`.

plt.show()

## Multi-Omic Oncology (`TCGA-BRCA`, `TCGA-KIRC`) and Patient-Level Clinical Attribution

To verify that the same architectural principles generalize beyond neuroimaging to molecular oncology and clinical tabular medicine, @tbl-real-cohorts-summary compares all `{python} N.n_models_word` models across the six real cohorts, @fig-multiomics-and-patient-attribution illustrates cross-cohort performance alongside exact patient-level clinical risk decomposition (`Diabetes` Patient #1 and `Heart` Patient #122 in @fig-heart-audit), and @fig-nsa-v-interpretability demonstrates how `nsa_flow` preserves localized hierarchical basis weights across modalities.

import os
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.datasets import load_diabetes
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from pysimlr import simlr

csv_path = "results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_path):
    csv_path = "paper/results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"

df = pd.read_csv(csv_path)
df["Model"] = df["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11.2, 4.1), dpi=300, gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1.3, 1.0]}, constrained_layout=True)

real_dsets = ["ADNI-MCI", "MultiOmics", "TCGA-KIRC", "Diabetes", "Heart", "mfeat"]
disp_names = ["ADNI-MCI\n(MRI→Cog)", "TCGA-BRCA\n(ER Acc)", "TCGA-KIRC\n(Stage Acc)", "Diabetes\n(Prog R²)", "Heart\n(CAD Acc)", "mfeat\n(Digit Acc)"]

piv_r = df[df["Dataset"].isin(real_dsets)].pivot_table(index="Dataset", columns="Model", values="Strictly_Linear_Metric", aggfunc="mean").reindex(real_dsets)

x = np.arange(len(real_dsets))
w = 0.20
ax1.bar(x - 1.5*w, piv_r["LEND"], w, label="LEND", color="#0284c7", edgecolor="#0f172a", lw=0.7)
ax1.bar(x - 0.5*w, piv_r["Flow-SiMR-V"], w, label="Flow-SiMR-V", color="#0d9488", edgecolor="#0f172a", lw=0.7)
ax1.bar(x + 0.5*w, piv_r["SiMLR"], w, label="SiMLR", color="#7c3aed", edgecolor="#0f172a", lw=0.7)
ax1.bar(x + 1.5*w, piv_r["PCA"], w, label="Dense PCA", color="#94a3b8", edgecolor="#0f172a", lw=0.7)

ax1.set_xticks(x)
ax1.set_xticklabels(disp_names, fontsize=8.2, weight="bold")
ax1.set_ylabel("Out-of-Sample Linear Probe Score (↑)", fontsize=9.5, weight="bold")
ax1.set_title("A. Multi-View SiMR vs. Dense PCA Across Real Cohorts", fontsize=10.0, weight="bold")
ax1.set_ylim(0.10, 1.05)
ax1.grid(True, axis="y", linestyle="--", alpha=0.35)
ax1.legend(loc="upper left", ncol=2, fontsize=8.0, frameon=True)

# Panel B: Exact Patient-Level Feature Attribution on Diabetes
np.random.seed(42)
data = load_diabetes()
X_scaled = StandardScaler().fit_transform(data.data)
res_db = simlr([X_scaled[:, :5], X_scaled[:, 5:]], k=2, positivity="positive", sparseness=0.5, random_state=42)
v_db = np.asarray(res_db["v"][0])
x_sample = X_scaled[0, :5]
impact = x_sample * v_db[:, 0]
feat_names = ["Age", "Sex", "Body Mass Index", "Mean Blood Pressure", "Total Cholesterol"]

idx = np.argsort(np.abs(impact))[::-1]
colors = ["#dc2626" if impact[i] >= 0 else "#0284c7" for i in idx]
y_pos = np.arange(len(idx))
ax2.barh(y_pos, impact[idx], color=colors, edgecolor="#0f172a", height=0.58, lw=0.7)

min_imp = float(np.min(impact))
max_imp = float(np.max(impact))
span = max(max_imp - min_imp, 0.5)
ax2.set_xlim(min_imp - 0.30 * span, max_imp + 0.30 * span)

for pos_i, orig_i in enumerate(idx):
    val_i = float(impact[orig_i])
    if val_i >= 0:
        ax2.text(val_i + 0.03 * span, pos_i, f"{val_i:+.2f}", va="center", ha="left", fontsize=8.4, weight="bold", color="#0f172a")
    else:
        ax2.text(val_i - 0.03 * span, pos_i, f"{val_i:+.2f}", va="center", ha="right", fontsize=8.4, weight="bold", color="#0f172a")

ax2.invert_yaxis()
ax2.set_yticks(y_pos)
ax2.set_yticklabels([feat_names[i] for i in idx], fontsize=8.5, weight="bold")
ax2.axvline(0, color="#0f172a", lw=0.9)
ax2.set_xlabel("Exact Additive Contribution (x_ij · v_jl)", fontsize=9.5, weight="bold")
ax2.set_title("B. Exact Patient-Level Risk Attribution (Patient #1)", fontsize=10.0, weight="bold")
ax2.grid(True, axis="x", linestyle="--", alpha=0.35)

plt.show()

```{python}
#| label: fig-nsa-v-interpretability
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "**Hierarchical Sparse Basis Localization (`varimax + nsa_flow`).** `LEND` loadings of each `Heart` and `Diabetes` view after Varimax rotation, the non-negative `nsa_flow` retraction ($w = 0.50$) and a per-component $q = 0.50$ quantile threshold; G is the Gini coefficient of each component. Computed at build time from `results_cache/nsa_v_loadings.json` (`scripts/paper_nsa_v_loadings.py`)."
import json, os
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from paper_numbers import CACHE
NSAV = json.load(open(os.path.join(CACHE, "nsa_v_loadings.json")))

def _gini(x):
    x = np.sort(np.abs(np.asarray(x, float)))
    n = len(x)
    return 0.0 if x.sum() == 0 else float(np.sum((2 * np.arange(1, n + 1) - n - 1) * x) / (n * x.sum()))

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(9, 8.5))
for ax, (cohort, view) in zip(axes.ravel(), [(c, v) for c in ("Heart", "Diabetes") for v in NSAV[c]]):
    d = NSAV[cohort][view]
    v = np.array(d["v"])
    order = np.lexsort((-v.max(1), v.argmax(1), (v.max(1) <= 1e-4).astype(int)))
    v, rows = v[order], [d["rows"][i] for i in order]
    ax.imshow(v, cmap="viridis", vmin=0, vmax=0.95, aspect="auto")
    for (i, j), val in np.ndenumerate(v):
        ax.text(j, i, f"{val:.2f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=9,
                color="black" if val > 0.5 else "white")
    ax.set_xticks(range(v.shape[1]), [f"L{j + 1}\nG={_gini(v[:, j]):.2f}" for j in range(v.shape[1])])
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(rows)), rows)
    ax.set_title(f"{cohort}: {view}", fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
:::
::::

In `MultiOmics` (`TCGA-BRCA`, $N = 822$), out-of-sample Estrogen Receptor classification accuracy on the linear entrypoint is `{python} N.brca_Flow_SiMR_V_pm` (`Flow-SiMR-V`), `{python} N.brca_LEND_pm` (`LEND`) and `{python} N.brca_NEDPP_pm` (`NEDPP`), against `{python} N.brca_PCA_pm` for `PCA` (3-seed means $\pm$ SD); the sparse non-negative dictionaries $\mathbf{V}_m$ are examined feature by feature in Appendix A. In `TCGA-KIRC` ($N = 467$), pathologic stage classification on the consensus embedding $\mathbf{U}$ is `{python} N.kirc_LEND_u_pm` for `LEND` against `{python} N.kirc_PCA_u_pm` for `PCA`. On compact clinical cohorts, `Diabetes` reaches $R^2 =$ `{python} N.diab_SiMLR` for `SiMLR` against `{python} N.diab_pca` for `PCA`, and `Heart` reaches accuracy `{python} N.heart_NSAFlow_PCA` for `NSAFlow-PCA` and `{python} N.heart_SiMLR` for `SiMLR`. @fig-nsa-v-interpretability shows the Varimax-rotated `nsa_flow` loadings ($q = 0.50$) of each `Heart` and `Diabetes` view, and the linear entrypoint $\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}} = \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ decomposes any individual patient's score into exact feature-level contributions $c_{m,i,j,l} = x_{m,i,j} v_{m,j,l}$ without post-hoc Monte Carlo approximations [@Wachter_2017; @karimi2021algorithmic; @pearl2009causality] (@fig-multiomics-and-patient-attribution B and @fig-heart-audit). Complete parameter sensitivity ablations—the $w \in [0.01, 0.95]$ trade-off curve, row-mean/ICA preprocessing controls, latent rank $k \in \{2, 3, 5, 8, 12\}$ scaling, and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests against `PCA`—are in Appendix B.
